mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLK 200/220 CDI OM646 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the OM646 is widely regarded as one of Mercedes' most durable diesel engines. With proper maintenance, examples have reached 500,000 miles without major failures. However, injector seal failure ("Black Death") is a known weakness, and timing chain stretch can occur on higher-mileage units. OM646 is a robust and durable workhorse. Injector seal failure is the most common issue - catch it early. Timing chain stretch can occur from 100,000 miles. Regular oil and filter changes every 10,000 miles are critical for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What is the "Black Death" problem on the Mercedes CLK 200/220 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: "Black Death" is the common term for injector seal failure on Mercedes CDI engines. When the seals fail, unburnt diesel and exhaust gases escape, creating a hard, tar-like carbon buildup around the injector seats. Symptoms: chuffing noise from engine bay, black residue around injectors. If ignored, injectors can seize and cylinder head damage can occur. Specialist seal replacement costs £250-£450. Catch it early - the repair is far cheaper than engine replacement.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes CLK 200/220 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Well-maintained OM646 engines regularly exceed 150,000-200,000 miles. With meticulous maintenance, some have reached 500,000 miles without major failures. OM646: 150k-200k+ miles with regular servicing. Injector seal failure typically occurs from 80,000-150,000 miles. Timing chain stretch risk from 100,000-200,000 miles. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles significantly extends life.

mainEntity.name: How much does timing chain replacement cost on a Mercedes CLK 200/220 CDI?

If the chain has already slipped, full engine replacement at £2,200-£3,500 is required. Specialist preventative chain replacement: £800-£1,300. Dealer pricing for same work: £1,200-£1,800. acceptedAnswer.text: On a CLK 200/220 CDI worth £2,500-£5,000, specialist engine replacement at £1,500-£2,500 is worthwhile if the body and interior are in excellent condition. mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CLK 200 CDI and CLK 220 CDI engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both use the same OM646 engine family. The CLK 200 CDI is a lower-power version (102-125 hp) while the CLK 220 CDI produces 150 hp. The difference is primarily in engine mapping and turbocharger specification, not mechanical hardware. Same engine block, cylinder head and bottom end. Power difference is electronic mapping and turbo spec. Reliability is identical between the two variants. Replacement engines are interchangeable with correct ECU programming.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes CLK 200/220 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes CLK 200 CDI and CLK 220 CDI arrived with the second-generation C209 CLK in the mid-2000s, powered by the OM646 2.1-litre four-cylinder common-rail turbodiesel. These engines offered a compelling blend of refinement and economy, making the CLK accessible to a wider audience than the petrol V6 and V8 variants.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes CLK 200/220 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The OM646 2.1-litre turbodiesel in the CLK 200 CDI and CLK 220 CDI is widely regarded as a durable and reliable workhorse - with properly maintained examples reaching 500,000 miles without major failures. However, like any diesel engine of its era, it has known weak points: injector seal leakage (the infamous "Black Death"), timing chain stretch, and turbocharger wear. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Injector Seal Failure ("Black Death") - The Most Common OM646 Problem
problems.rootCause: Injector seals fail, allowing unburnt diesel fuel and exhaust gases to escape past the seal. This creates a hard, tar-like carbon buildup around the injector seats - a condition commonly referred to as "Black Death." Symptoms include a chuffing noise from the engine bay, visible black residue around injectors, and rough running.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace injector seals, clean injector seats, new clamp bolts. Requires specialist removal tools
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-150k miles; effective if caught before seat damage

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Injector Seat Re-cutting & Seal Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Re-cut injector seats, replace seals and clamp bolts with upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if seat damage has occurred; prevents recurrence

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit fully rebuilt OM646 engine with new injectors, seals, and timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if Black Death has caused cylinder head damage or injector seizure

problems.recommendation: Injector seal failure is the single most common issue on the OM646 engine. Don't ignore the tell-tale chuffing noise or black residue. Specialist injector seal replacement at £250-£450 is cost-effective and resolves the issue. However, if the engine has been run with leaking seals for an extended period, cylinder head damage may have occurred - in which case a rebuilt engine with new injectors and upgraded seals is the safer option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM646 Mercedes CLK 200/220 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - The OM646's Hidden Weakness
problems.rootCause: The double roller timing chain can stretch over time, particularly with extended oil change intervals. Symptoms include rattling on cold start, rough running, and in severe cases, the chain jumping teeth and causing catastrophic valve/piston contact.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; tensioner wear only

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Full Timing Chain & Sprocket Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets
Supply & fit fully rebuilt engine with new timing components, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has slipped and valves have contacted pistons

problems.recommendation: Rattling on cold start is the early warning sign. Don't ignore it - specialist timing chain replacement at £800-£1,300 resolves the issue if done promptly. The OM646 is otherwise a robust engine, and replacing the timing chain before failure can extend engine life significantly.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM646 timing chain replacement for your Mercedes CLK 200/220 CDI

problems.h4: Turbocharger Wear & Boost Leaks - Power Loss and Limp Mode
problems.rootCause: Turbocharger bearing wear and oil residue in the intake system can cause loss of boost pressure. Boost leaks from pipes between the turbo and inlet manifold are also common, triggering limp mode and power loss.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspect and replace leaking intercooler pipes, hoses and clamps
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; simple fix

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and replace turbocharger with reconditioned unit, new oil feed lines
repairOptions.longevity: 120k-180k km; effective if caught before engine damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit fully rebuilt engine with new turbo, injectors, and timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo debris has circulated through the engine

problems.recommendation: Loss of power and hissing noises are classic signs of a boost leak. Start with a simple inspection of intercooler pipes - often a £100-£200 fix. If the turbo itself has failed, specialist replacement at £700-£1,200 is cost-effective. However, if turbo debris has contaminated the oil system, full engine replacement is the only safe route.
